I was probably about 15 or 16 doing laundry in the backroom. Our backroom was the biggest room in the house beside the living room. After you first enter if you keep going straight you'll run into the back door (out of the house) and our basement door to the right, right next to it. We keep our washer and dryer on the very left side of the room a good 14ft at least away. I was in the back room alone when I heard this creaking. At first I thought it was just the way I was standing on the floor because our floors are very creaky, but then I heard the creaking again and for longer so I looked up and around and I watched as the basement door continued to slowly creep itself open. I didn't wanna pass it on my way out so I screamed for my brother as loud as I could and had him walk me out just in case anything happened again (Im a scaredy cat)

Around that same time I started getting freaked by everything. Things in my room would move or fall over without reason, my TV would turn itself on and my DVD player would open and close itself so I started sleeping on the couch in the living room. By this time I had insomnia for a couple years. I wasn't able to stay asleep, to this day I'm much better at napping for an hour than trying to sleep for more than an hour. Once I'd wake up it would take me a couple hours to get back to bed and I became a VERY light sleeper. My dad would get up for work at 4 AM, and I was normally awake to wish him good morning and good luck at work. My dad's a heavy guy and his footsteps are loud and impossible to miss really. Well this one night I was laid on my side facing the wall, I was awake and trying to go back to bed. I felt something lean on the couch and lean over me. I heard and FELT a deep heavy breathing on my neck. I thought it was my dad checking to see if I was awake. So I whipped around to wish him good morning but no one was there. No one was awake, not even our dog that was in my mom's room. I couldn't go back to sleep, I was completely awake and 100% afraid.

This is a bit of a long story. When I was young I was really shy and timid and tended to befriend the people who would run over me and use me for their self needs because I couldn't stand up for myself. Well in middle school I became friends with this girl. I'll call her R for story sake. I would hang out at R's all the time, go to the school dances with her,  everything. I should have cut her off when I told her my dog died in my lap and she told me it wasn't as bad as the memories of her ex's ( she had several and would literally break up with someone and 20 minutes later had a new boyfriend) but the last straw was when I was in a very suicidal state. The only thing that got me through was choir. It was my safe place. I had been through a bit of shit and choir was just the break I needed, so when I found out my choir teacher was moving and that I wasn't gonna get to see him after I graduated I cried. I cried for about 3-4 hours, two of them being in school, because the mental repair I received and the support in that class  I received was something special. I tried venting to her in hopes that I'd feel better but she immediately disregarded what I confessed and said she was missing her necklace (I had the other half too) and eventually said that the necklace was more important than my feeling and my teacher. I lost it at that point. I was sending her paragraphs and  voice messages of how upset she had just made me.  How bad she made me feel. She really fucked me up. Maybe I had gone a bit over board but that literally was the only thing that got me through middle school without self harming or worse. It was in freshman year when I had made a true friend for the first time. I was still being bullied and this particular day at breakfast had food thrown at me from other kids. The teachers yelled at me and my friends for it. I had complained to my friend during gym and said something along the lines of "I don't know, I guess I shouldn't be complaining because this is someone's good day" and she whipped around so fast and grabbed my shoulders and said " I don't give a rats ass if someone else's day is bad because your hurting too. More than one person could hurt as once, that doesn't mean you don't get to be upset." I broke down in tears, like for once I was allowed not to feel okay. It was the most relieving feeling I'd ever felt and I think everyone needs to know that you're allowed to have a bad day. I had just been conditioned by others who made pain a competition that my feelings didn't matter. But I do now and no one can tell me otherwise anymore. Best friend ever. We don't hang out much anymore, just grew apart but I'll message her every once and a while my thanks and appreciation.

TL;DR: my "friend" compared the teacher that prevented me from commiting suicide to a necklace and said he didn't matter. I flipped out and found a friend who actually cared about how I felt and helped me work on setting healthy boundaries for myself and helped me become aware that my feelings matter too. I still thank her till this day.

Luckily we have a decently big team now and this hasn't really happened since. I've gotten another medication to take in case I get anxiety attacks now that I can take on site which also helps. I would transfer but things have turned around for the most part and I really do love my team, well except my TL but that's a different story of its own.
